input.command: git status && git branch -vv && git log -5 --oneline && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD@{upstream} 2>/dev/null; git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null; git merge-base HEAD origin/master 2>/dev/null; ls -la
git remote -v; git log --oneline -3; git branch -a; ls -la .github 2>/dev/null; ls PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md 2>/dev/null; node -v

mkdir -p /opt/cursor/artifacts scratch
node smoke.ts > /opt/cursor/artifacts/smoke.log 2>&1
node scratch/check.ts > /opt/cursor/artifacts/check.log 2>&1
cat /opt/cursor/artifacts/smoke.log /opt/cursor/artifacts/check.log
git status
git diff -- impl.ts
ls artifacts

cat > /opt/cursor/artifacts/code-tour-author-handoff.md << 'EOF'
<decision> Full bank details go to team leads and to support agents with an open payout ticket on the same merchant; other support views stay last-four; engineers and merchant-id mismatches get none. That matches the ticket’s payout-problem framing and the named last-four fallback, instead of treating any ticket topic as enough or showing engineers masked digits. </decision>
<risk> If the intended rule is “any open ticket for the merchant” rather than payout-only, refund/account tickets will be masked instead of full. Engineer-none is also a product call the ticket never named. </risk>
<verified> `node smoke.ts` loaded `showBankDetails` and returned a BankView. `node scratch/check.ts` covered team-lead full, support payout full, support no/other/refund ticket masked, engineer none, merchant mismatch none, and unique audit ids. </verified>
EOF
git add impl.ts artifacts && git commit -m "Implement ticket" && git status && git log -1
